System Network

Connectivity between chromatographic systems

Source: vignettes/network.qmd

Network Overview

The network shows how chromatographic systems are connected through pairwise models. Each node is a system and each edge a model between two systems (models are directional: one per source/target pair). Models are only built between systems of the same method type (reversed-phase with reversed-phase, HILIC with HILIC), since the elution order differs between the types.

Metric Value
Total Systems (Nodes) 328
Total Models (Edges) 49,570
Models between RP systems 49,570
Average Models per System (as source) 151.1
Network Density 46.22%

Network Visualization

Each point is a system, sized by its number of compounds; the shape shows the method type. Hover over a system to see its name and group; the letters of the named groups are explained in the table below the plot.

How close two systems are is measured by their similarity: the Jaccard index of their compounds, i.e. shared compounds divided by the compounds in either system. Unlike the number of shared compounds, it does not make every system look close to the few very large ones. The systems are placed using only the links with a similarity of at least 0.4, so that systems sharing most of their compounds end up together. All pairs sharing at least 20 compounds are then drawn, wider and darker the more similar they are, so weak links fade into the background. The slider hides the links below a chosen similarity.

The colours are groups of systems that share many compounds, found from all pairs. Dark bundles between groups are many pairs of systems in two groups that share a fair part of their compounds.

The groups mostly reflect which lab submitted a series of systems measured with the same set of standards; where a lab’s standards are distinctive, the kind of compounds shows through. Six groups were named by hand (see the table below). The groups are recomputed whenever the data change, so a group gets a name only when it still matches the named group: at least half of its systems belong to the named group, and at least half of the named group’s systems are in it. Other groups are shown as unnamed.

Named Groups

The groups were named from the studies that contributed their systems (titles from their DOIs) and the chemical classes (ClassyFire) of their compounds, using the RepoRT data of October 2026. A further group of 69 systems, mostly metabolomics of human, plant and food samples from many labs, could not be given a convincing name. The member lists are in inst/extdata/system_groups.csv.

Group Name Systems (Oct 2026) Basis
A Drug, pesticide and contaminant screening, with the Witting lab (BGC) method series 102 67 systems are one Witting lab series (Dataset - BGC: the same ~850 standards, lipids, bile acids, metabolites and some pesticides, across columns, acetonitrile levels and MS modes); almost all others are screening of pharmaceuticals, drugs of abuse, pesticides and environmental contaminants, plus the METLIN SMRT library of synthetic molecules
B Plant and food natural products 33 21 systems from Data sharing in PredRet for accurate prediction of retention time: application to plant food bioactive compounds (Food Chem 2021); others from plant metabolomes, apple and honey phenolics, natural product dereplication and Chinese herbal medicine; compounds mainly terpenoids, flavonoids, alkaloids and coumarins
C Endogenous metabolite standards, Folberth et al. 2020 (positive mode) 37 All from MS2 and LC libraries for untargeted metabolomics (J Chromatogr B 2020, doi:10.1016/j.jchromb.2020.122105): the same standards on 37 methods, positive ionisation
D Endogenous metabolite standards, Folberth et al. 2020 (negative mode) 37 As C, negative ionisation
E Emerging contaminants, Kruve lab (Souihi et al. 2022) 28 All from MultiConditionRT: predicting liquid chromatography retention time for emerging contaminants for a wide range of eluent conditions (J Chromatogr A 2022, doi:10.1016/j.chroma.2022.462867): one standard mix under 28 eluent conditions
F Emerging contaminants, retention index set (Aalizadeh et al. 2022) 6 All from the Thomaidis lab retention index based on the cocamide diethanolamine homologous series (Anal Chem 2022, doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02893): pesticides, pharmaceuticals and other contaminants
